text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card, but the conclusion is poorly grounded and internally contradictory. The card shows 99215 at 13.5% vs expected 3.8% (ratio 3.53, ~194 excess claims) and the provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every complexity stratum (e.g., 9.2% vs 4.1%, 18.2% vs 8.0%, 33.3% vs 11.9%, 51% vs 21.8%). The summary leans toward 'high acuity panel' and says 'near-peer', which misrepresents this. The next step claims 'the documentation returned supports the level billed' although zero records were returned. The two cited claims are high-complexity examples that only support the sicker-panel point, and none of the 25 low-complexity 99215 claims is cited, so an investigator gets one-sided support. Missing documentation is mentioned but not turned into a next step.","problems":["Next step says 'documentation returned supports the level billed' but the card shows 0 documented claims and the summary itself says no records came back; fabricated/contradictory","Headline 'near-peer 99215 rate on patients with no conditions (4.1% vs 2.8%)' is selective; the provider is above peers in every stratum, ~1.5x at 0 conditions and 2x+ at 1-5+ conditions","Leaning 'pattern_consistent_with_high_acuity_panel' is not supported given the risk-adjusted ratio of 3.53 and the excess of ~194 claims; the rationale concedes 'still above peers within high strata'","Recommends not pursuing recovery without any documentation review; should recommend requesting records for the visits instead","Cited claims are only the two high-complexity examples; no low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., 0 conditions with R10.9, J06.9, Z09) are cited, so the concerning evidence is omitted","Rationale says 'No records requested' while the next step implies records were reviewed, which is inconsistent","The 24% of 99215 on 0-1 condition patients is stated without context or comparison"]}
